cities.name: Brussels
interests: Historic Squares & Medieval Streets 🏛️ — Grand city boulevards, ornate guild houses and royal architecture.
Art, Comics & Culture 🎨 — Tintin murals, Art Nouveau gems and unforgettable museums.
Gastronomy & Chocolate 🍫 — Waffles, frites, pralines and cozy café culture.
cities.local_food_tip: Try Belgian waffles with different toppings, crispy frites with dozens of sauces, moules-frites, stoofvlees (Flemish beef stew), and pralines from iconic chocolatiers like Neuhaus or Godiva.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🏛️ Grand Place: One of Europe's most breathtaking squares, surrounded by ornate 17th-century guild houses covered in gold trim. In the early morning, the square is quiet, making it perfect for photos of the Gothic Town Hall and the King's House. As sunlight hits the façades, the gold details glow warmly, revealing fine carvings and statues. This is a place to slow down, walk in circles, notice the different guild symbols, and imagine the marketplace that stood here centuries ago. → 👣 Wander the Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert: A magnificent 19th-century glass-roofed arcade filled with chocolatiers, cafés and boutique shops. Every detail — the glass ceiling, arches, sculptures — feels like stepping into the elegance of old Europe. Grab a morning coffee and praline here. → 🧇 Stop by Maison Dandoy for iconic waffles, freshly baked and incredibly fragrant. Afternoon: 🖼️ Mont des Arts: This elevated cultural district gives panoramic views over Brussels' rooftops. Gardens, staircases, musicians and fountains create a lively atmosphere. The Museums of Fine Arts nearby are ideal for art lovers. → 🏛️ Head to the Royal Palace: Walk around the grand façade and the surrounding Warandepark, a peaceful green escape in the city. → 🍽️ Lunch in the Sablon area at Le Pain Quotidien or a nearby brasserie, enjoying local dishes with a cozy Belgian ambiance. Late Afternoon: 🏰 Visit the Atomium: A futuristic icon built for the 1958 World Expo. The mirrored spheres reflect the sky and the city, and inside you find exhibitions, long escalators and 360° views. → 🌉 Nearby, stroll around Mini-Europe, a fun miniature park featuring Europe’s landmarks. Sunset: 🌇 Walk back toward the city center or stay near Atomium, where the metallic sphere begins to glow with evening lights. The reflections are perfect for photos. Night: 🌃 Place Sainte-Catherine: Lively seafood restaurants, illuminated squares and a relaxed evening vibe. Try moules-frites paired with Belgian beer from a local bar.

ideas: 🌸 Stroll through Warandepark as flowers bloom and locals enjoy the sun.
🎨 Street musicians and open-air art displays around Mont des Arts.
☕ Outdoor cafés in Sablon with pastries and warm sunlight.
🌅 Golden sunsets at Grand Place with long evening light.
🎶 Open-air concerts around the Royal Palace gardens.
🍦 Ice cream and cold drinks along Sainte-Catherine on warm nights.
🍁 Fall colors in city parks like Parc de Bruxelles.
🥐 Cozy cafés perfect for pastries and hot chocolate.
🏛️ Museum visits during chilly or rainy afternoons.
🎄 Winter Wonders Market with lights and wooden stalls.
✨ Grand Place illuminated in magical festive colors.
☕ Hot chocolate tastings in iconic chocolatiers.

public_transport_tips: 🚇 Brussels Metro is fast and convenient — ideal for major attractions.
🚶 The old center is fully walkable.
🚋 Trams are useful for reaching Atomium and farther districts.
📱 Plan routes via STIB: https://www.stib-mivb.be

cities.name: Bruges
cities.local_food_tip: Try Bruges chocolate from artisan shops, Belgian waffles, frites, waterzooi (creamy stew), and speculoos cookies.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🌉 Start at the picture-perfect Rozenhoedkaai: One of Europe’s most photographed waterfront spots. Early morning light reflects softly on the canals, giving the medieval towers a magical glow. You can capture mirror-like reflections of gabled houses and stone bridges before crowds appear. → 🚤 Take a canal boat tour departing from Huidenvettersplein: The guide explains history and architecture while you drift slowly along the waterways. The perspective from water level reveals hidden courtyards and ivy-covered brick walls. → ☕ Warm up with hot chocolate at The Old Chocolate House — rich, creamy, unforgettable. Afternoon: 🏛️ Continue to Belfry Tower (Belfort): Climb 366 steps for breathtaking views of red rooftops and market squares. Every level of the tower reveals medieval mechanics, old bells and wooden beams. At the top, the panoramic wind hits your face and the entire old town spreads beneath you like a postcard. → 🏰 Walk to Burg Square: Home to the Gothic Town Hall and the Basilica of the Holy Blood. Superb architecture, mosaics and carved façades make this square a delight for slow exploration. → 🍽️ Lunch at Gran Kaffee De Passage for Belgian classics. Late Afternoon: 🌳 Visit Beguinage (Begijnhof): A peaceful white-washed courtyard dating back to the 13th century. Walking here feels like entering a monastery garden frozen in time; the silence and trees create a calming, protected space. → 🧀 Stop by a local chocolate boutique for pralines. Sunset: 🌇 Head back to Rozenhoedkaai for evening photos when lights reflect on the still canal. Night: 🌃 Dinner near the Markt square and a final slow walk through lantern-lit cobblestone streets — Bruges at night feels like a living fairy tale.

ideas: 🚤 Longer canal tours under golden sunset.
🌅 Evening strolls around Markt and Burg.
🍨 Ice cream shops open late on warm nights.
🥐 Cozy cafés for pastries and warm drinks.
🏰 Museums and quiet old town corners perfect for colder days.
✨ Fairy-tale holiday lights in narrow alleys.
🧇 Hot waffles and mulled wine stalls.

public_transport_tips: 🚶 Bruges is fully walkable — no need for buses.
🚴 Rent a bike to explore parks and windmills.
🚂 The train station is a 15-minute walk from the old town.
📱 Use Belgian Rail (SNCB) app for connections: https://www.belgiantrain.be

cities.name: Ghent
cities.local_food_tip: Try Gentse Waterzooi, neuzeke (candy), Belgian chocolate, fries and local craft beers.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🏰 Begin at Gravensteen Castle: A dramatic 12th-century fortress rising above the rivers. Explore stone rooms, towers and medieval artifacts. The ramparts give amazing views of the old town — rooftops, bridges, and canals. Early morning is peaceful and the grey stone shines in soft light. → 🌉 Walk to Graslei & Korenlei: Two gorgeous riverside streets with ornate guild houses. Sit by the water to watch boats glide past as students gather with coffee. Afternoon: ⛪ Head to the Saint Bavo’s Cathedral: Home of the world-famous “Adoration of the Mystic Lamb” painting. The cathedral interior is breathtaking with high ceilings and detailed altars. → 🖼️ Explore Werregarenstraat, the graffiti alley: Colorful, creative and constantly changing. → 🍽️ Lunch at Mosquito Coast, known for global flavors. Late Afternoon: 🚤 Take a river cruise from Graslei: A calm, scenic ride revealing more secret corners of Ghent. → 📚 Wander around the university district — youthful, vibrant, full of creative shops and cafés. Sunset: 🌇 Head back to Graslei. As lights reflect on the water, the medieval façades glow warmly. Night: 🌃 Enjoy Ghent nightlife — bars around Oude Beestenmarkt and Veldstraat are full of energy.

ideas: 🚤 Calm boat rides with fresh breezes.
☕ Terraces filled with students enjoying the sun.
🎶 Street music around the medieval center.
🍺 Summer beer festivals across the city.
🎄 Christmas market in the old center.
✨ Light trails reflecting in the river.

public_transport_tips: 🚶 The center is walkable.
🚋 Trams connect major spots — use De Lijn app.
🚲 Bikes are popular among students; easy to rent.
📱 Plan routes: https://www.delijn.be

city_events.description: 🎉 One of Europe’s biggest cultural city festivals with music, theater and street art.

cities.name: Antwerp
cities.local_food_tip: Try Antwerpse Handjes cookies, Belgian chocolate, fries, shrimp croquettes, and local beers.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🕍 Start at Cathedral of Our Lady: A towering Gothic masterpiece with Rubens paintings inside. Morning light shines through tall stained-glass windows, creating magical colors inside the nave. The surrounding square has cafés and artists painting small scenes of old Antwerp. → 🏙️ Walk to Grote Markt: Guild houses with gold ornaments line the square, and the Brabo Fountain tells the legendary tale of Antwerp’s origins. Afternoon: 🖼️ Visit Museum aan de Stroom (MAS): A massive red-stone museum with amazing city and port views from its rooftop. The exhibitions cover maritime history, world cultures and Antwerp's global trade. → 🎨 Explore the trendy Eilandje district with cool cafés and modern architecture. → 🍽️ Lunch at Balls & Glory or a harbor-side restaurant. Late Afternoon: 💎 Walk to the Diamond District: Countless shops and workshops showcase Antwerp’s jewelry heritage. Even if you’re not buying, it’s fascinating to see the craftsmanship. → 🛍️ Stroll down Meir Street for shopping. Sunset: 🌇 Go up to the MAS rooftop for orange-pink skies above the harbor. Night: 🌃 Enjoy fashion-district bars or dinner in the old town.

ideas: 🌸 Blossoms in old squares and cathedral courtyards.
☕ Coffee terraces in the fashion district.
🚶 Long walks along the Scheldt river.
🍦 Ice cream along the river promenade.

public_transport_tips: 🚂 Antwerp Central Station is an attraction itself — stunning architecture.
🚋 Trams and buses run frequently.
🚶 Old town is walkable.
📱 Use De Lijn app for routes: https://www.delijn.be

city_events.name: Antwerp Fashion Week
city_events.description: 👗 A major event showcasing Belgian and international designers.

cities.name: Leuven
cities.local_food_tip: Try Belgian beers, waffles, speculoos, frites and local pastries.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🏛️ Begin at Leuven Town Hall: A masterpiece of Gothic architecture with hundreds of statues and intricate details. The façade is incredibly ornate, and early morning light highlights each small carving. → 📚 Walk to the University Library & Tower: A symbol of Leuven’s academic history. The reading rooms are atmospheric, filled with wooden shelves, and the tower offers beautiful views. Afternoon: 🌳 Stroll through Groot Begijnhof: A peaceful UNESCO-listed quarter with cobblestone lanes, bridges and brick houses. Walking here feels like stepping into an old monastic village. → 🍽️ Lunch at a student-friendly café near Oude Markt. Late Afternoon: 🍺 Visit Stella Artois Brewery for a tour. Learn about Leuven’s beer tradition and enjoy tasting. → 🛍️ Wander around the shopping district, full of bookstores and boutiques. Sunset: 🌇 Sit at Oude Markt, often called the 'longest bar in Europe'. Night: 🌃 Enjoy student nightlife around the central squares.
public_transport_tips: 🚶 Walkable old center.
🚲 Bikes are very popular.
🚍 Buses reach outer districts.
📱 Route planning via De Lijn.

city_events.name: Leuven Beer Week
city_events.description: 🍺 A week dedicated to Belgian brewery culture.

cities.name: Liège
cities.local_food_tip: Try Liège waffles (caramelized sugar crystals inside), meatballs in syrup sauce, and local beers.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🌊 Start at La Boverie Park: Beautiful riverside scenery, ideal for slow morning walks. → 🖼️ Visit the La Boverie Museum, located inside the park — modern art and elegant interiors. Afternoon: ⛪ Head to Saint Paul’s Cathedral: Impressive Gothic columns and peaceful atmosphere. → 🏛️ Walk to Place Saint-Lambert and the nearby shopping streets. → 🍽️ Lunch at a brasserie offering Liège specialties. Late Afternoon: 🏙️ Climb the Montagne de Bueren: 374 steps leading to panoramic city views. The climb is steep but rewarding, and the rooftops and river bend make for stunning photos. Sunset: 🌇 Golden-hour views from the top of Bueren. Night: 🌃 Dine near the river or explore lively bars around the university district.

ideas: 🎄 Christmas Village — one of Belgium’s oldest markets.

public_transport_tips: 🚶 Most central spots are walkable.
🚍 Buses connect the wider city.
🚂 Liège-Guillemins Station is a modern architectural icon.
📱 TEC app for planning routes.

city_events.name: Liège Christmas Village
city_events.description: 🎄 One of Belgium’s most atmospheric holiday markets.

cities.name: Mons
cities.local_food_tip: Try local cheeses, Belgian beers, waffles, and pastries.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🏛️ Start at Mons Grand-Place: Elegant square with cafés and 17th-century façades. Early morning makes the atmosphere serene and perfect for photography. → 🐒 Touch the lucky monkey statue at Hôtel de Ville — a local tradition. Afternoon: 🏰 Visit the Mons Belfry: The only Baroque belfry in Belgium with panoramic city views from the top. The surrounding garden is peaceful and perfect for a break. → 🎨 Explore the BAM Museum for modern art exhibitions. → 🍽️ Lunch in a brasserie near Grand-Place. Late Afternoon: 🌳 Walk through Parc du Château: Lovely hilltop park with views. → ☕ Coffee at a small local café. Sunset: 🌇 Enjoy warm light from the Belfry viewpoint. Night: 🌃 Dinner on Grand-Place with its illuminated façades.

ideas: 🍁 Orange leaves around Parc du Château.

public_transport_tips: 🚶 Old town is compact and walkable.
🚍 Buses cover outer districts.
🚂 Easy train trips from Brussels.
📱 Use TEC for planning routes.

cities.name: Namur
cities.local_food_tip: Try Namur’s pâté, waffles, frites, beer and river-view restaurants.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🏰 Start at the iconic Citadel of Namur: A massive fortress on a hill overlooking the Meuse River. Wander the walls, tunnels and viewpoints — each terrace shows a different panorama of the city and the river bend. Early morning is especially peaceful, and the mist sometimes rises from the water, giving the citadel a mystical atmosphere. → 🌉 Walk down to Pont de Jambes: Classic bridge views perfect for photography. Afternoon: 🕍 Visit the Saint Aubin’s Cathedral: Unique Baroque architecture and a bright, elegant interior. → 🍽️ Lunch in the old town — many places serve regional dishes paired with local beers. Late Afternoon: 🌳 Stroll through Parc Louise-Marie: Lakes, bridges and quiet paths perfect for relaxation. → ☕ Stop at a cozy café nearby. Sunset: 🌇 Return to the citadel viewpoints for golden-hour river views. Night: 🌃 Enjoy dinner in old streets or near the waterfront.

ideas: 🌅 Long golden sunsets over the Meuse River.
🍁 Red and gold forests around the citadel.
📸 Misty morning photos from the hill.
✨ Calm river views in cold air.

public_transport_tips: 🚶 Old center is walkable.
🚍 Buses help access hills and outskirts.
🚂 Good train links to Brussels & Liège.
📱 Use SNCB app for train planning.

city_events.name: Namur Festival
city_events.description: 🎭 Open-air performances, music and cultural shows across the city.
